messages.content: What are the components of Civil Law?

message.content:
Civil law, also known as civil jurisprudence or civil law system, is a legal framework that governs non-criminal disputes between private parties. Its components can be broadly categorized into several key areas: | Component | Description | |-----------|-------------| | **Legal Sources** | • **Statutes & Codes** – Written laws enacted by legislatures (e.g., Civil Code, Commercial Code).
• **Case Law / Judicial Precedent** – Decisions from higher courts that guide lower courts.
• **Customary Law** – Long‑standing practices recognized as binding.
• **International Treaties & Agreements** – When applicable, they may influence domestic civil law. | | **Core Areas of Law** | • **Contract Law** – Rules governing agreements, obligations, and remedies for breach.
• **Tort Law** – Liability for wrongful acts causing harm or loss.
• **Property Law** – Rights and duties related to real and personal property.
• **Family Law** – Marriage, divorce, child custody, alimony, etc.
• **Inheritance & Succession Law** – Distribution of estates after death.
• **Commercial Law** – Business transactions, company formation, bankruptcy. | | **Procedural Elements** | • **Jurisdiction** – Which court has authority over a case.
• **Venue** – Physical location where a case is heard.
• **Pleadings & Filings** – Complaint, answer, motions, discovery.
• **Evidence Rules** – Admissibility, burden of proof.
• **Remedies** – Damages, injunctions, specific performance. | | **Legal Principles** | • **Good Faith & Fair Dealing** – Parties must act honestly.
• **Equitable Remedies** – Courts may grant non-monetary relief.
• **Doctrine of Res Judicata** – Final judgments cannot be re‑litigated.
• **Doctrine of Estoppel** – Prevents parties from contradicting prior statements. | | **Institutions** | • **Courts** – Trial courts, appellate courts, supreme courts.
• **Legal Professionals** – Lawyers, judges, notaries.
• **Regulatory Bodies** – Bar associations, professional licensing boards. | | **Enforcement Mechanisms** | • **Judicial Enforcement** – Court orders, garnishment, seizure.
• **Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR)** – Mediation, arbitration, conciliation. | These components work together to provide a structured, predictable, and fair system for resolving disputes among individuals, businesses, and other entities.
